stem:
A term baby is born through meconium-stained amniotic fluid. The baby cries immediately, has good tone and a heart rate of 150 beats/min, and breathes comfortably without signs of airway obstruction.

What is the most appropriate immediate airway plan?

options.label: A
options.text: Routine oropharyngeal suction before skin-to-skin care
options.explanation: Routine suction provides no benefit in a vigorous unobstructed baby and can cause harm. Meconium exposure alone is not an indication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A vigorous baby does not need routine laryngoscopy or tracheal suction. These procedures add risk without improving outcomes in this situation.

options.label: C
options.text: No routine suction; skin-to-skin care with observation
options.explanation: The baby is breathing effectively and has good tone and heart rate. Continue routine supportive care and observe for respiratory compromise because of the meconium exposure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PPV supports inadequate breathing; it is not a method for clearing meconium. This baby already has effective spontaneous respiration.

options.label: E
options.explanation: CPAP is used when respiratory support is clinically needed. Meconium in the fluid without respiratory distress does not itself justify CPAP.

context: A vigorous meconium-exposed newborn does not need routine suction; provide routine care and observe breathing.
